semantic_correction.stem: An adult is admitted to a hospital unit because of a primary behavioral health condition. Which nursing action best reflects current Joint Commission suicide-risk standards?

options.A: Use a validated tool to screen for suicidal ideation, and if the result is positive, follow the organization’s evidence-based suicide-risk assessment process.
options.B: Wait for the client to disclose suicidal intent during the interview, then begin formal screening if the client describes a specific plan or recent attempt.
options.C: Use an unstructured clinical interview for suicide screening, and reserve a validated tool for clients whose behavior suggests a higher level of suicide risk.
options.D: Apply the same suicide-screening requirement to all hospitalized clients, regardless of whether their primary reason for care is behavioral or medical.

semantic_correction.rationale: Joint Commission National Performance Goal #8 states that hospitals must screen patients being treated primarily for a behavioral health condition for suicidal ideation using a validated screening tool and use an evidence-based process to assess patients who screen positive. Current Joint Commission FAQs reinforce that the requirement applies when behavioral health is the primary reason for care and that the National Performance Goal does not require universal suicide screening of every hospital patient. Therefore A is correct. B incorrectly delays screening until spontaneous disclosure or a specific plan or attempt. C substitutes an unstructured interview for the required validated screening tool in this population. D overstates the requirement as universal for all hospitalized clients regardless of presentation.
semantic_correction.educational_objective: For a hospital client whose primary reason for care is a behavioral health condition, use a validated suicide-ideation screening tool and follow an evidence-based suicide-risk assessment process when the screen is positive, without misrepresenting the standard as universal screening of every hospital patient.
semantic_correction.source_document_title: National Performance Goal #8: Reducing the Risk for Suicide; Standards FAQs — Screening Requirements and Use of an Evidence-based Process to Assess Risk
semantic_correction.source_version_date: Current 2026 National Performance Goal context; screening FAQ last updated April 21, 2026; evidence-based assessment FAQ last updated April 22, 2026; non-psychiatric applicability FAQ last updated June 24, 2026; live pages rechecked August 20, 2026
semantic_correction.source_locator: NPG #8 Standards: hospitals must screen all patients being treated primarily for a behavioral health condition for suicidal ideation using a validated screening tool and use an evidence-based process to assess patients who screen positive. HAP/CAH Screening Requirements FAQ: the NPG does not require universal screening of all patients. Evidence-based Process FAQ: patients who screen positive require an in-depth evidence-based assessment process that determines and documents overall suicide risk. Applicability in Non-Psychiatric Settings FAQ: the requirements apply to a general-hospital patient being treated/evaluated for a behavioral condition as the primary reason for care and to patients expressing suicidal ideation during care.
semantic_correction.source_claim_supported: For hospital patients treated primarily for a behavioral health condition, Joint Commission requires suicidal-ideation screening with a validated tool and an evidence-based risk-assessment process after a positive screen; the NPG does not impose universal screening on every hospital patient regardless of presentation.
semantic_correction.blueprint_source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing (NCSBN)
semantic_correction.blueprint_locator: Psychosocial Integrity, printed p.10 (official PDF pageno 13): supports emotional, mental and social well-being of clients experiencing stressful events or acute/chronic mental illness; assess psychosocial factors influencing care and plan interventions; provide care and education for acute/chronic psychosocial health issues including depression; promote a therapeutic environment; assess potential for violence and use safety precautions.
semantic_correction.blueprint_topic: Psychosocial Integrity — suicide-risk screening and evidence-based follow-up assessment in behavioral health care
semantic_correction.correction_summary_append: RULE1 cleanup retained the Joint Commission suicide-screening construct, removed the absolute-word distractor pattern, balanced A/B/C/D length, and tightened the scope to primary behavioral-health presentations and evidence-based follow-up after a positive screen.

scope_exclusions.universal_screening: The item explicitly does not claim Joint Commission requires universal suicide screening for every hospitalized client.
scope_exclusions.positive_screen_management: The item tests the requirement for an evidence-based risk assessment after a positive screen; it does not prescribe one specific safety-plan intervention before risk is assessed.
scope_exclusions.tool_brand: No specific validated screening instrument is required by name in the item.
scope_exclusions.risk_level: No numeric score or specific high/moderate/low classification threshold is tested.
scope_exclusions.nonbehavioral_primary_reason: The stem is intentionally limited to a primary behavioral health condition because that is the direct screening requirement tested.
scope_exclusions.blueprint_precision: NCSBN Psychosocial Integrity does not explicitly use the words ‘suicide’ or ‘self-harm’ on the cited printed p.10 activity list; the mapping is based on psychosocial assessment, depression/mental-illness care, therapeutic environment, and safety-related assessment.

near_duplicate_check.note: Targeted GitHub search for ‘suicide screening validated tool behavioral health primary reason evidence-based assessment Joint Commission’ returned no indexed repository match. No broad bank scan was performed.

option_audit.A: Correct. It exactly combines the validated screening requirement for the stated population with evidence-based assessment after a positive result.
option_audit.B: Plausible because intent, plan, and attempt history are important in suicide-risk assessment, but the validated screening step is not deferred until those findings are volunteered.
option_audit.C: Plausible because clinical interviewing remains important, but an unstructured interview does not replace the validated screening-tool requirement for this population.
option_audit.D: Plausible because suicide risk can occur in medical populations, but Joint Commission does not require universal screening of every hospital patient under this NPG.

ambiguity_check: No second defensible best answer. A alone matches both required steps for the stated primary-behavioral-health population. B delays screening, C replaces the validated screening method, and D overgeneralizes the population scope.

cueing_check.note: The key is tied with C rather than uniquely longest; all four are parallel nursing actions with comparable detail and no ‘only/always/never/every’ distractor cue.

blueprint_audit.entry_level_relevance: Screening and responding to psychiatric/behavioral health risk is consistent with entry-level RN psychosocial assessment, care of clients with depression or other mental illness, therapeutic environment, and safety-related assessment.
